name: Chapter 2 - Measuring prices and inflation - Comprehensive MCQ Bank

questions.text: A price index compares:

options.a: the quantity of a basket at two dates without using prices
options.b: nominal GDP with population
options.c: the price level of the same basket at a given date with its price level at a chosen baseline date
options.d: the income approach to GDP with the expenditure approach

questions.text: For a single product i, the basic price index at date t with baseline a is:

options.a: p_it / p_ia
options.b: p_ia / p_it
options.c: (p_it + p_ia)/2
options.d: p_it − p_ia

questions.text: At the baseline date a, a basic price index expressed in base 1 must equal:

options.b: the inflation rate
options.d: 100 regardless of the chosen base convention

questions.text: An index in base 100 is obtained from the corresponding base-1 index by:

options.a: subtracting 1 and multiplying by 100
options.b: multiplying it by 100
options.c: dividing it by 100
options.d: adding 100

questions.text: If a base-1 price index is 1.18 in 2025 relative to 2020, the price in 2025 is:

options.a: 18 times the 2020 price
options.b: necessarily €1.18
options.c: 1.18 times the 2020 price
options.d: 0.18 times the 2020 price

questions.text: If a base-100 price index equals 93 in year t relative to the base year, the price level is:

options.a: unchanged because only 100 has an interpretation
options.b: 7% above its baseline level
options.c: 7% below its baseline level
options.d: 93% below its baseline level

questions.text: For a date t after the baseline a, the cumulative price growth rate from a to t using a base-1 index is:

options.a: P_t|a − 1
options.b: P_t|a
options.d: P_a|t − 1 only

questions.text: A price index is 1.25 in 2024 with 2020 as baseline. The cumulative inflation rate from 2020 to 2024 is:
A price index for 2012 is 1.20 when 2015 is the baseline. The growth factor of prices from 2012 to 2015 is:
If P_2012|2015 = 1.20, then from 2012 to 2015 prices changed by approximately:
The price growth factor from t1 to t2 can be computed from a common price-index series as:

options.a: P_t1|a / P_t2|a
options.b: P_t2|a − P_t1|a
options.c: P_t1|a + P_t2|a
options.d: P_t2|a / P_t1|a

questions.text: Suppose a price index equals 110 in 2022 and 121 in 2024, both with the same base year. Inflation from 2022 to 2024 is:
Changing the baseline year of a price index:

options.a: changes the numerical index levels but not the measured price growth factor between two given dates
options.b: changes both index levels and the true growth factor between any two dates
options.c: leaves all index levels unchanged
options.d: is impossible once the series has been published

questions.text: Why does the absolute level of a price index have meaning only relative to its baseline?

options.a: Because the index directly measures quantities rather than prices.
options.b: Because index levels are measured in euros.
options.c: Because all price indices have the same baseline by law.
options.d: Because it is a ratio comparing current prices with the chosen reference-price level.

questions.text: The fundamental problem when constructing a composite price index is:

options.a: how to convert all quantities into labour hours
options.b: how to weight the prices of different products in a single aggregate
options.c: how to eliminate all relative-price changes
options.d: how to ensure every product receives exactly the same economic importance

questions.text: A simple arithmetic average of product prices may have questionable economic meaning because:

options.a: products can differ greatly in economic importance and units, yet an unweighted average treats them symmetrically
options.b: an average always uses base-year quantities
options.c: it necessarily equals a Laspeyres index
options.d: prices cannot mathematically be averaged

questions.text: A weighted composite price index gives a larger influence to a product when:

options.a: its price is numerically smaller
options.b: it was introduced more recently
options.c: it is imported
options.d: the product has a larger weight in the relevant basket

questions.text: A Laspeyres price index uses:

options.a: current-period quantities as weights
options.b: future quantities expected by households
options.c: base-period quantities as fixed basket weights
options.d: equal weights for all products

questions.text: The Laspeyres price index at t relative to a is:

options.a: Σ p_it q_it / Σ p_ia q_ia
options.b: Σ p_it q_ia / Σ p_ia q_ia
options.c: Σ p_ia q_it / Σ p_it q_ia
options.d: Σ q_it / Σ q_ia

questions.text: The interpretation of a Laspeyres index equal to 1.30 is that:

options.a: every single price rose by exactly 30%
options.b: the current-period basket contains 30% more goods
options.c: real consumption rose by 30%
options.d: the base-period basket costs 30% more at current prices than it cost in the base period

questions.text: In the course example, the 2018 reference basket has quantities (100, 50, 40) and costs 3000 in 2018. If the same basket costs 3550 in 2019, the 2019 Laspeyres index is approximately:
A Laspeyres index holds the basket composition fixed in order to:

options.a: eliminate the need for a baseline
options.b: force every product price to have the same weight
options.c: isolate how the cost of a given reference basket changes as prices change
options.d: measure changes in current quantities only

questions.text: The Belgian CPI described in the course is:

options.a: a GDP deflator limited to exported goods
options.b: a stock-market index
options.c: a Laspeyres-type index tracking a broad basket of household goods and services
options.d: an index of domestic producer profits only

questions.text: The slides state that the Belgian CPI basket contains approximately:

options.a: 520 goods and services divided into 12 categories
options.b: all goods produced in Belgium regardless of household consumption
options.c: only food and energy products
options.d: 12 goods divided into 520 categories

questions.text: Since 2006, the Belgian CPI basket composition is reviewed:

options.a: once every ten years only
options.b: only when inflation exceeds 10%
options.c: yearly
options.d: daily

questions.text: The purpose of regularly updating the CPI basket is to:

options.a: ensure all prices receive equal weights
options.b: make inflation independent of consumer substitution
options.c: keep the reference basket closer to current household consumption habits
options.d: turn the CPI into the GDP deflator

questions.text: The Belgian "Indice Santé" is based on the CPI basket but excludes:

options.a: services and durable goods
options.b: food, housing and medical care
options.c: all imported products
options.d: alcoholic beverages, tobacco products and motor fuels

questions.text: The Harmonised CPI is designed mainly to:

options.a: measure only Belgian export prices
options.b: make inflation measures more comparable across EU countries using harmonised basket rules
options.c: calculate purchasing power parity with one product
options.d: replace national accounts GDP

questions.text: The Belgian HCPI weights shown in the slides sum to:

options.a: 1 only because it cannot be expressed in per mille
options.d: 1000 per mille

questions.text: A product category with a larger HCPI weight will, for a given percentage price change:

options.a: have a smaller impact by construction
options.b: have a larger direct impact on measured HCPI inflation
options.c: affect only real GDP, not inflation
options.d: have no impact because the index is unweighted

questions.text: When using a composite price index, measured inflation can differ across indices because:

options.a: inflation is independent of the reference basket
options.b: different weighting conventions give different importance to individual price changes
options.c: all composite indices must use identical weights
options.d: only basic price indices can be used to calculate growth rates

questions.text: Changing the reference year of a composite Laspeyres-type index can affect measured inflation because:

options.a: the reference year can imply a different set of expenditure weights
options.b: the index no longer has a baseline
options.c: the basic mathematical growth-factor formula becomes invalid
options.d: all prices are converted into quantities

questions.text: The CPI and GDP deflator can evolve differently because:

options.a: they cover and weight different sets of prices
options.b: the CPI is always equal to the GDP deflator in an open economy
options.c: the GDP deflator excludes all domestic production
options.d: one measures quantities and the other unemployment

questions.text: Which statement is most accurate?

options.a: Every valid price index must yield exactly the same inflation rate.
options.b: There is no single convention-free inflation number when different composite price indices use different baskets and weights.
options.c: Changing a basket affects only the index level, never measured inflation.
options.d: Only changes in energy prices can make inflation measures differ.

questions.text: Laspeyres price indices are generally considered to have an upward bias in measured inflation partly because they:

options.a: systematically use future prices
options.b: treat falling prices as rising prices
options.c: do not fully adjust for improvements in product quality
options.d: exclude all durable goods

questions.text: If a product's price rises by 8% while its quality improves substantially, a price index that ignores quality change may:

options.a: understate inflation by exactly 8%
options.b: automatically correct the price using GDP per capita
options.c: overstate the pure inflation component of the price increase
options.d: measure only quantity growth

questions.text: The "new product bias" arises because new products are often added to a CPI basket:

options.a: with zero weight forever
options.b: before they exist
options.c: only after their prices have risen permanently
options.d: only after they become widely consumed, potentially missing earlier price declines

questions.text: The substitution bias in a fixed-basket index arises because:

options.a: the index excludes all goods with rising prices
options.b: consumers shift toward relatively cheaper goods, while the fixed basket continues to weight the original consumption pattern
options.c: consumers never respond to relative prices
options.d: the index uses current quantities every period

questions.text: If the price of one good rises sharply relative to substitutes, actual consumers may reduce purchases of it. A fixed Laspeyres basket will tend to:

options.a: convert the price increase into real wage growth
options.b: understate inflation because it immediately lowers the good's weight
options.c: be unaffected by the good's price
options.d: overstate the increase in the cost of maintaining consumers' adapted consumption pattern

questions.text: Annual basket revisions reduce substitution bias because they:

options.a: update weights to reflect changed consumption patterns, although substitution within the year can still be missed
options.b: make the basket completely flexible at every instant
options.c: remove all quality-measurement problems
options.d: force all consumers to buy the reference basket

questions.text: In macroeconomics, a real variable is:

options.a: a variable measured only in physical units and never monetary units
options.b: a nominal variable adjusted for the aggregate evolution of prices
options.c: a variable that is simply observed rather than expected
options.d: a variable that excludes all taxes

questions.text: The generic way to obtain a real variable from a nominal monetary variable is to:

options.a: divide the nominal variable by an appropriate price index
options.b: add the price index
options.c: multiply it by the inflation rate
options.d: subtract the nominal interest rate

questions.text: For a single good with nominal expenditure v^n_it = p_it q_it and price index P^i_t|a = p_it/p_ia, the real expenditure is:

options.a: p_ia q_it
options.b: p_it q_it
options.c: p_it/p_ia
options.d: q_it/p_it

questions.text: Why does the growth rate of a correctly deflated real variable for a single good depend only on quantities?

options.a: Because the same reference price multiplies quantities at both dates and cancels in the growth ratio.
options.b: Because nominal prices are assumed never to change.
options.c: Because all goods have unit prices.
options.d: Because the baseline date must equal both comparison dates.

questions.text: Changing the reference date used to express a real variable:

options.a: changes both its level and its quantity growth factor
options.b: changes its level but not its growth factor between two given dates
options.c: has no effect on its level
options.d: turns the variable nominal

questions.text: For an aggregate nominal variable v^n_t and an aggregate price index P_t|a, the associated real variable is:

options.a: P_t|a / v^n_t
options.b: v^n_t − P_t|a
options.c: v^n_t × P_t|a
options.d: v^n_t / P_t|a

questions.text: The real wage is defined as:

options.a: the wage divided by real GDP
options.b: the nominal wage plus inflation
options.c: the nominal wage multiplied by the CPI
options.d: the nominal wage divided by a consumption price index

questions.text: The economic interpretation of the real wage is:

options.a: the firm's total labour cost including all capital income
options.b: the purchasing power of the nominal wage in terms of the reference consumption basket
options.c: the worker's hours worked
options.d: the worker's nominal tax rate

questions.text: A worker's nominal wage rises by 5% while the relevant price index rises by 8%. The worker's real wage:

options.a: falls
options.b: is unchanged
options.c: rises by 13%
options.d: rises by 3%

questions.text: A worker's nominal wage rises by 12% while consumer prices rise by 7%. The worker's purchasing power:

options.a: cannot be assessed without the GDP deflator specifically
options.b: is unchanged because both variables increased
options.c: falls because any positive inflation lowers real wages
options.d: rises because nominal wage growth exceeds price growth

questions.text: A CPI with base year 2010 equals 140 in 2024. If a worker's nominal wage rose only 25% over the same period, then relative to 2010 the worker's real wage has:

options.a: decreased
options.b: remained unchanged
options.c: increased
options.d: become impossible to measure without changing the base year

questions.text: A price index equals 80 in 2018 and 100 in 2020. What was the cumulative inflation rate from 2018 to 2020?
A price index equals 150 in 2020 and 165 in 2022. The price growth factor from 2020 to 2022 is:
An item costs €48 in the base year and its base-100 index is 125 today. Its current price is:
An item costs €60 today and its base-100 price index is 120. Its base-year price was:
A basket contains 2 units of good A and 1 unit of good B in the base year. Base-year prices are €10 and €20; current prices are €15 and €22. The Laspeyres price index in base 1 is:
Suppose a nominal salary is €3,000 and the relevant base-1 CPI is 1.25. The real salary in base-year purchasing-power units is:
(Select the incorrect answer) A well-constructed answer about inflation measurement should recognise that:

options.a: price-index levels depend on the chosen baseline
options.b: different baskets can yield different measured inflation rates
options.c: a composite price index is completely independent of its weighting rule
options.d: growth between two dates can be calculated by taking a ratio of index values

questions.text: The chapter explicitly distinguishes measuring inflation from explaining inflation. Its conclusion is that:

options.a: inflation can only arise from measurement bias
options.b: the construction of the CPI itself explains all causes of inflation
options.c: once a price index is built no macroeconomic model of inflation is needed
options.d: price indices measure how the aggregate price level evolves, while later chapters analyse mechanisms causing those movements
